body.estimand_functional: \(\mathcal R(C)=\{D\in\mathfrak S_p:\mathsf S(D)=\mathsf S(C)\}\), with \(\mathsf S(E)=(\operatorname{skel}(G_E),\operatorname{uc}(G_E),(\mathcal N_j(E))_{j\in V},F(E))\)

sampling_model.design: Population equality of full positive-definite covariance models is the identification kernel; the statistical rung uses independent Gaussian sampling and global BIC over the finite labelled state class.
sampling_model.units: Each observation is one independent realization of the \(p\)-variable centered linear Gaussian SEM.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment in the structure-identification theorem; the prespecified pairs in \(\mathcal Q\) index downstream interventions and responses.
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; every innovation variance is positive and otherwise unrestricted.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For each candidate state and positive-definite sample covariance, target-local block-incidence matrices define positive-definite Gram systems whose unique solutions estimate the common coefficient in each parent block; strictly positive constrained residual variances estimate the innovation variances. The effect maps apply these same off-model block-constrained solutions before taking finite path sums and derivatives. A deterministic measurable fallback invokes no Gram inverse, likelihood supremum, or derivative when \(S_n\) is singular, and all asymptotic claims run through integers \(n\geq p\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 5.17 proves structural identifiability within BPEC-DAGs, whose edge-colour classes all have size at least two, while Question 5.19 asks for a graphical characterization of edge-coloured model equivalence.
Theorem 2 transforms any pair of equivalent DAGs through exactly their distinct disagreeing edges, each reversed while covered.
Theorem 4.1 characterizes partial-homoscedastic model equivalence by ordinary Markov equivalence and fixed parent sets for vertices in nonsingleton variance blocks.
Theorem 4.4 characterizes existence and uniqueness of the MLE in a fixed compatibly coloured RDAG through augmented-sample linear independence.
The essential graph uniquely represents each ordinary DAG Markov-equivalence class and has chordal chain components.
The paper gives polynomial-time counting and uniform sampling for ordinary Markov equivalence classes by clique-picking on chordal components.
The paper gives linear-delay enumeration of ordinary Markov-equivalent DAGs, including fixed-background-knowledge variants.
The paper establishes BIC-type asymptotic model choice for finitely many smoothly curved submodels of an exponential family.
IDA consistently estimates the multiset of possible total effects across an ordinary Markov-equivalence class.
The paper constructs resampling-and-screening confidence intervals for one fixed true causal effect after constraint-based graph discovery.
The paper derives efficient least-squares estimators and joint covariance calculations for total effects under a known linear causal graph.

body.tldr: Equal incoming coefficients encode communities of direct causes. BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 makes those communities structurally identifiable by excluding singleton blocks, but admitting singleton causes restores genuine observational equivalence and leaves the correct quotient unknown. The project characterizes equality of the full positive-definite covariance models exactly: two target-blocked states agree if and only if their skeletons, unshielded colliders, repeated parent blocks, and orientations across unequal endpoint block families agree, equivalently if and only if singleton-block covered reversals with partition transport connect them. Tangent-support recovery and an exact sparse covariance separator supply the coefficient-specific necessity; Chickering's monotone transformation then yields a shortest path. The same quotient gives complete finite enumeration, generic fixed-\(p\) BIC component recovery, and simultaneous inference for its finite set of total effects, while output-sensitive enumeration of distinct rational effect maps remains open.

project_justification.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 proves BPEC structural identifiability only after forbidding singleton edge-colour classes and explicitly leaves graphical and transformational edge-coloured equivalence open. Ordinary covered reversals ignore coefficient partitions, while partial homoscedasticity constrains innovation variances rather than incoming coefficients.
project_justification.niche: Target-local blocked colourings with unrestricted positive noise variances form a natural intermediate class: repeated blocks reveal stable causal communities, but singleton blocks retain exactly the ordinary orientation ambiguity compatible with those communities.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the repeated-block invariant from the model tangent at the identity, proves by a sparse regression separator that reversed edges must join equal endpoint families, and combines these facts with monotone covered reversals to obtain an if-and-only-if static and transformational characterization plus its statistical quotient consequences.

body.related_work: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 is the writing and primary method anchor: its Introduction frames equal incoming coefficients as causal communities, Theorem 4.1 proves smooth model geometry, Proposition 5.4 and Corollary 5.6 provide edge-colour faithfulness, Theorem 5.17 proves identifiability only for proper blocked colourings, and Questions 5.19--5.20 plus the Discussion leave graphical and transformational equivalence open. Chickering1995, Theorem 2 and its Find-Edge proof, supplies the disagreement-decreasing sequence of distinct covered reversals; the new first step is proving every selected arrow is a singleton block and its endpoint partitions coincide on common parents. WuDrton2023, Theorem 4.1, is the closest complete partition-constrained analogue: it fixes parent sets at vertices sharing a nonsingleton innovation-variance block, whereas the present invariant recovers labelled repeated incoming coefficient blocks and orientations across unequal endpoint families. MakamReichenbachSeigal2023 studies likelihood geometry and least-squares MLEs for a fixed compatibly coloured RDAG, not equality of covariance images across graph orientations. AnderssonMadiganPerlman1997 and the two 2023 Wienobst papers provide ordinary essential-graph, counting, and enumeration machinery; transported target partitions are absent. Haughton1988 informs the finite smooth-model BIC argument, with exact-image quotienting and algebraic intersection removal derived here. MaathuisKalischBuhlmann2009, ChangGuoMalinsky2026, and GuoPerkovic2022EfficientLS inform possible-effect estimation and post-discovery inference, but do not cover every member of a blocked full-model-equivalence effect set.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The population component \(\mathcal R(C)\) is an equivalence class of complete covariance-model images, not the pointwise fibre of every state fitting one exceptional covariance. Zero edges and coincident coefficients can create additional pointwise representations outside the component. The fixed directed set \(F(C)\) records orientations forced directly by unequal nonsingleton families, but ordinary collider and acyclicity constraints can compel further arrows. Neither fact identifies a numerical coefficient merely because its arrow is compelled.
body.honest_scope: The equivalence theorem concerns finite labelled causally sufficient linear Gaussian DAGs, target-local coefficient blocks, unrestricted real block coefficients, unrestricted positive target-specific innovation variances, and full positive-definite covariance images. It does not cover cross-target edge colours, vertex-coloured innovation variances, latent confounding, selection, cycles, or pointwise supermodel fibres. The BIC and confidence procedures use deterministic measurable fallbacks at singular sample covariance, while their limits concern integers \(n\geq p\), for which \(S_n\) is positive definite almost surely. These results are fixed-\(p\), pointwise, and generic away from a proper algebraic exceptional set; no greedy-search consistency or uniform inference near model intersections is asserted. In the all-singleton case the exact reduction is ordinary DAG Markov equivalence, and in the no-singleton case the component is a singleton.
